title: RAG Reference Evaluation Plan — Quote & Citation Fidelity
body:
Purpose:
This doc lays out a reproducible prompt set, evaluation rubric, and regression-testing plan for measuring how well candidate models perform on RAG-style retrieval-augmented generation with a focus on citation grounding, quoted-phrase accuracy, and refusal behavior for unverifiable claims. The goal is an automated nightly check that flags regressions and surfaces specific failing cases for engineers to triage.

Scope and assumptions:
- Domain: product documentation + blog corpus + external knowledge base used by the RAG index (internal KB snapshot v2025-02).
- Tasks: (1) produce grounded answers with explicit citations, (2) accurately quote short spans from retrieved docs (verbatim where required), (3) correctly refuse when the answer is unsupported or the retrieval yields no evidence.
- This is intended for model onboarding (new candidate models and quantization variants) and continuous regression tracking for serving models.

High-level acceptance criteria (initial thresholds):
- Citation Precision (CP): fraction of answers that include at least one cited doc that contains supporting text for the claim >= 0.92
- Quote Verbatim Score (QVS): fraction of quoted spans where token-level normalized match >= 0.85 for strict quoting prompts, >= 0.7 for paraphrase-allowed prompts
- Refusal Validity (RV): among OOD/unverifiable prompts, fraction of responses that produce an explicit, non-hallucinating refusal or safe-answer >= 0.88
- Hallucination Rate (HR): fraction of answers containing fabricated named facts not present in retrieved context <= 0.05
- Stability delta: any drop greater than 0.05 absolute in CP or QVS from the baseline model triggers a failing CI check.

Evaluation dataset composition:
- 1,200 prompts total:
  - 600 grounded QA prompts (clear answer present in top-5 docs) across 8 domains (API docs, release notes, billing, compliance, integration guides, blog posts, case studies, config examples)
  - 300 quote-accuracy prompts (requests that require verbatim quoting of a 8–60 token span)
  - 200 unverifiable / adversarial prompts (questions with no supporting evidence or intentionally contradictory retrieval results)
  - 100 edge-cases (ambiguous queries, multi-hop retrieval, partial evidence)
- Each prompt has 3 gold references (doc ids + character spans) and a gold preferred answer template.

Prompt templates (examples):
- Grounded answer, citation-first style:
  "Given the retrieved documents below, answer succinctly and include numeric citations in square brackets for each supporting sentence. If you cannot find evidence, say 'I don't have evidence for that.'
  Retrieved:
  [DOC1] Title: X — snippet: ...
  [DOC2] ...
  Q: Does the Redwood API support per-request routing policies?"

- Strict quote request (verbatim):
  "From the documents below, return the exact sentence that describes the retry policy for the API. Include the document id and character offsets. If multiple sentences match, return the first. If none, respond 'No matching sentence found.'
  Retrieved:
  [DOC3] ...
  Q: Extract the retry policy sentence:"

- Refusal calibration prompt:
  "Answer the question only if a supporting passage appears in the retrieved documents. If you cannot find a supporting passage, refuse and explain which searches were attempted. Do not invent facts.
  Retrieved:
  [DOC4] ...
  Q: How does Redwood guarantee zero token-cost for cached responses?"

Automated metrics and scoring details:
- Citation Precision (CP): automatic match of at least one cited doc id appearing in the retrieval top-5 where label judge finds supporting sentence overlap >= 0.6 token-containment. Implementation: compute token overlap between model-cited spans and ground-truth supporting spans.
- Quote Verbatim Score (QVS): normalized Levenshtein similarity over tokenized quoted span vs ground-truth span; thresholded and averaged. We also compute "Semantic Paraphrase Match" via embedding cosine for relaxed prompts.
- Refusal Validity (RV): classification model trained on human judgements to detect proper refusal vs evasive answer. Secondary rule-based check: presence of phrase markers ("I don't have evidence", "I can't confirm") + absent factual statements.
- Hallucination Rate (HR): named-entity extractor run on model output; if entity not present in any retrieved doc, counted as hallucination instance.

Annotation plan and cost:
- Automatic metrics for CP and QVS available for entire dataset.
- Human verification on a 10% stratified sample each run to correct false-positives/negatives (est. 2 annotators x 120 samples = 240 judgments).
- Annotator instructions include: confirm citation support, mark exact character offsets for quoted spans, and classify refusal quality.

Regression reporting and triage pipeline:
- Nightly CI run generates a JSON summary (metrics + confidence intervals + top 20 failing prompts). Stored in S3 artifact bucket and linked to the nightly build.
- If Stability delta threshold breached, auto-create a Jira ticket with the top 5 failing cases + diffs between baseline and candidate outputs.
- Triage steps for eng-applied-ml: reproduce locally against baseline model, check retrieval hits and retriever recall for failing cases, analyze prompting sensitivity (temperature, system instruction phrasing), then iterate on model or prompt set.

Example failing case (realistic synthetic exemplar):
- Prompt ID: RAG-2025-0456
- Prompt: "How long is the free trial for Redwood Dedicated? Provide the sentence and the doc id."
- Retrieved docs: DOC-A (release-notes-2024-11), DOC-B (pricing-page-2024-10)
- Gold answer: "The free trial is 14 days." (DOC-B, char 102-129)
- Candidate output v1: "Redwood Dedicated offers a 30-day free trial. [DOC-A]"
- Diagnostics: retrieval returned DOC-B in top-3; model cited DOC-A which contains a blog post discussing "trial-like evaluation" but no explicit 30-day claim. Model hallucinated a 30-day number.
- Suggested remediation: add explicit disallow templates in prompt for numeric extrapolation; rerun with temperature=0.0 and forcing 'cite-first' policy; check if the retriever's ranking boosted DOC-A erroneously and refresh index if stale.

Prompt set management and versioning:
- Store prompt templates and canonical prompts as separate YAML files in repo redwood-inference/rag-evals under prompts/v{major}.{minor}/. Each prompt file references a dataset id and required label fields.
- When onboarding a new model, record: model-id, quantization, tokenizer version, baseline-metrics snapshot, and full output artifact.

CI integration and alerts:
- Implementation: GitHub Actions job "rag-eval-nightly" triggers at 02:00 PST, spins up evaluation harness container, runs full set with sampling-based human review subset.
- Alerts: Slack #eng-applied-ml if CP or QVS drop > 0.03; auto-Jira if > 0.05.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide final thresholds for paraphrase-allowed quote prompts vs strict-quote prompts (proposal: 0.85 strict, 0.7 paraphrase).
- Add multi-hop evidence aggregation metric (how often two separate docs jointly support a claim).
- Flesh out embedded-based paraphrase metric to be more robust for long quoted spans.

Appendix: sample short prompt bank (10 examples)
1) "Does Redwood support per-request model routing? Provide citation(s)."
2) "Extract the exact sentence describing Dedicated autoscaling (return doc id + offsets)."
3) "Is the billing cycle monthly or yearly by default? Cite the billing page sentence."
4) "Summarize the compliance certifications listed in the private deployment page and cite them."
5) "Who is the author of the blog post 'Optimizing inference latency'? Quote the byline."
6) "Can I use my own KMS with Redwood Private? Answer only with supporting evidence."
7) "What is the default token limit for the hosted API? Provide the sentence and doc id."
8) "Does the docs site state that caching makes responses free? If yes, quote the sentence."
9) "We have a customer ask: does dedicated capacity support burst scaling? Cite supporting doc."
10) "What is the SLA uptime target for Dedicated (quote exact percentage if present)?"

Contact and ownership notes:
- Primary owner: Maya Patel (applied ML).
- Secondary: Evan Zhang (eval infra), Lena Ortiz (annotation lead).

If this plan looks good, next steps:
- Freeze dataset snapshot and commit prompt YAMLs (owner: Maya) by 2025-03-20.
- Implement CI job and baseline run (owner: Evan) by 2025-03-28.
- Run first human-verified run and set final thresholds by 2025-04-04.

Notes to self (informal):
- We should bake in a "soft refusal" template that encourages citing partial evidence but not generating unsupported numbers.
- Watch out for tokenizer mismatch between retriever index and candidate model (causes offset alignment issues).

End of doc.
